title: C++
summary: C++ is a high-level, general-purpose language created by Bjarne Stroustrup as an extension of C, first released in 1985. It supports multiple paradigms including procedural, object-oriented, functional, and generic programming. The language is designed for systems and embedded programming, emphasizing performance, efficiency, and flexibility. C++ is usually implemented as a compiled language with multiple vendor-provided compilers. It is standardized by ISO, with the latest standard ISO/IEC 14882:2024 (C++23) ratified in October 2024. C++ has been widely used for software infrastructure, video games, servers, and performance-critical applications.

mechanisms.title: Multi-paradigm design
mechanisms.explanation: C++ was designed from the start to support multiple programming paradigms—procedural, object-oriented, functional, and generic—allowing programmers to choose the best style for the task while maintaining performance. This flexibility is a core design goal rather than a retrofitted feature.

mechanisms.title: Compiled implementation
mechanisms.explanation: C++ is typically implemented as a compiled language, meaning source code is transformed into machine code by vendor-provided compilers (e.g., GCC, Clang, MSVC). This enables low-level memory manipulation and direct hardware access, which supports its use in systems programming and resource-constrained environments.
